findings.location: vectors.json (transcripts); scripts/i05_gate_channel_v2.py Gate._record / STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT; README P1 and P2 rows, Decision 10
findings.finding:
Four stated v2 rules are not pinned by any vector. I replayed 34 single-rule source mutants against all 198 pinned checks; 26 were caught. These four survived:
- 'restart keeps a pending drain'. No vector issues a DRAIN_REQUEST and then a GATE_RESTART while the drain is pending. The README says a restart drops a pending drain without an answer.
- 'DRAIN_STARTED on every request'. No vector sends two WRITE_BEGINs while one is pending. The README says it is recorded once.
- 'DELETE UID from this execution's CREATE of any manifest'. No vector arms a DELETE of manifest M2 with the UID created for M1. The README says the UID must be for the same manifest.
- 'drain answer computed before the DRAINED record'. This case cannot be reached with the model's failure injection: STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT always fails the next record, so after a first record succeeds it can only fail the first record of an event or the INVALIDATED record inside _storage_failure. It can never fail DRAINED alone, or a DENIED record after a CLOSED, INVALIDATED, EXPIRED or DRAIN_STARTED record that succeeded.
I added a finer injection in a reviewer subclass that fails the k-th upcoming record. With it the model behaves as stated:
- DRAINED fails after a durable TERMINAL: the drain is answered HELD and the marker is written.
- CLOSED or INVALIDATED succeeds and then DENIED fails: the response is HELD with deniedActionIds [1], and the restart is HELD.
- EXPIRED succeeds and then DENIED fails: denied [1].
- DRAIN_STARTED succeeds and then DENIED fails: denied [1], answer HELD.
The other four surviving mutants were not missing vectors: a redundant MANIFEST_REUSED digest check (a digest fixes the identity), RESTARTED read as a state record (not observable), the created-UID reset at BIND (redundant because the map is keyed by digest), and an unreachable 'ambiguous' branch in _settle_drain.

findings.location: README Decision 8 ('PENDING until no consumed action lacks a terminal record, then OPEN ... or HELD'); README P1 row ('W02c treats PENDING as wait, OPEN as the fence and HELD as no write'); Gate.fence, Gate._settle_drain
findings.finding:
Two wording issues in the drain-answer semantics:
(a) In HELD the drain is answered HELD at once, even while a consumed action has no terminal record. Probe PA-RR: CREATE in flight, DRAIN_REQUEST -> PENDING, CLOSE(RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) -> drain HELD with the CREATE still CONSUMED. T93 shows the same after PEER_CHANGED. The P1 row states this correctly (fence HELD first); Decision 8's wording does not. This fails safe.
(b) OPEN is answered once, on the settling event, and can come before the broker's seal and agreement check. T30, T87, T88 and T90 answer OPEN with the action TERMINAL but not yet sealed. After OPEN the generation can still become HELD, and nothing is signalled again:
- probe open-then-RR: OPEN, then CLOSE(RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) -> HELD;
- probe open-then-EOF-unsealed: OPEN, then CHANNEL_LOST -> fatal PEER_LOST HELD.
A3 is not violated: every consumed action has a durable TERMINAL record and A1 is closed. But an I07 implementer who reads the README as 'OPEN is the grant' would keep writing after the generation went HELD. The current I07 model already re-evaluates the fence and moves maintenance OPEN -> HELD (MAINT_HELD).
findings.requiredChange: Reword Decision 8 so that a HELD generation answers HELD at once. In the P1 row or under Still open (W02c-F), state that OPEN is a point-in-time answer: the gate can become HELD afterwards (RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, non-orderly channel loss with an unsealed action, storage failure), and the I07 writer must keep evaluating the fence after OPEN.

findings.finding:
The residual is disclosed correctly in substance; three points need precision.
(1) It needs two failed journal writes, not one: the failing record and the INVALIDATED STORAGE_FAILURE record written after the marker attempt. It also needs one failed marker write and no later state record before the restart.
- Probe PC-one-journal-fail-marker-fail: one journal failure plus one marker failure -> the INVALIDATED HELD record is durable -> restart HELD.
- Probe PC-residual-then-drain: a DRAIN_REQUEST after the double fault writes DRAINED HELD -> restart HELD.
(2) The argument 'the broker's own journal keeps that HELD' covers RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED only. In probe PC-residual-EOF (orderly CHANNEL_LOST whose CHANNEL_ENDED write fails twice, marker failed) the gate is HELD in memory for its own storage failure, no broker holds anything, and the restart comes back CLOSED.
(3) After such a restart, a fresh WRITE_BEGIN is answered OPEN (probe PC-residual-restart-then-drain). This is the I07 consequence carried as W02c R1. A3 is still met: in every divergence I found, all actions were sealed, terminal and non-ambiguous.
findings.requiredChange: State the residual's exact precondition: two consecutive journal write failures (the failing record and the INVALIDATED record), one failed marker write, no torn record, and no state record written before the restart. Say that it also covers the gate's own storage-failure HELD, not only RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED. Say that a WRITE_BEGIN after such a restart is answered OPEN, and link it to W02c R1.

findings.location: README Decisions 6 and 9; Gate._expire; Gate._settle_drain; base section 5 ('DRAINING: ... original authority bounds any already admitted work')
findings.requiredChange: State a bound on the forwarded upstream exchange, for example the execution's signed lifetime and the 900-second limit, after which the exchange is treated as lost (IO_AMBIGUOUS, HELD). Alternatively state that the broker must seal by its own deadline.
Restore these clauses, or name them explicitly as carried unchanged from the v1 README.

findings.finding:
Three hygiene items:
- Two manifests of one run with the same identity are refused with 'a manifest identity resolves to more than one run' (probe: run-one plus a second Pod digest named probe-pod). This is stricter than the README text, and the message is misleading.
- A priorBindings object without manifestDigests or manifestIdentities (v1 shape) raises KeyError instead of a refusal.
- byteFrames are listed B11, B14, B12, B13.
findings.requiredChange: Word the refusal as 'more than one manifest' (or document the within-run rule). Refuse an incomplete priorBindings explicitly. Order B12-B14.

P1.evidence:
Each v1 probe now behaves as the README says:
- PA with REVOCATION, EXPIRY, PEER_FAILURE, OBSERVATION_FAILURE and STORAGE_FAILURE: DRAIN -> PENDING; close -> INVALIDATED; UPSTREAM 201 -> drain OPEN with DRAINED INVALIDATED; STATUS drainPending false; ARM -> NOT_ACTIVE (T87-T89).
- PA with RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED: drain HELD on the close.
- PA3: close, then DRAIN -> PENDING, STATUS INVALIDATED drainPending true inFlight 1, upstream -> OPEN (T90). With UPSTREAM_LOST or an aborting seal -> HELD.
- Q3: seal refused STORAGE_FAILURE -> drain HELD at once, drainPending false (T91).
- CLOSED -> OPEN at once and HELD -> HELD at once (T92); fatal -> HELD (T93); ARM NOT_ACTIVE in INVALIDATED (T94).
The fence equals the I07 model's _fence. The remaining items are wording and W02c guidance: V2 and V4.

P2.evidence:
- created_uids is fed only by a CREATE 201 with a durable TERMINAL record. GET 200 no longer authorizes a DELETE (T47, T96, UID_NOT_CREATED).
- Probe PD is now config refusal K02. K03 refuses a run digest that is not in the profile.
- Probe PE is now MANIFEST_REUSED (T95: digest reuse and identity-only reuse). The BIND record carries the digests and identities.
- My campaign derived each later generation's priorBindings only from earlier journals' BIND records, over three generations including colliding runs and a re-used nonce. A shadow API-server world checked that no CREATE, GET or DELETE was forwarded for an identity created by another run, and that every armed DELETE UID came from this execution's own durable CREATE 201. 0 violations.
- Missing 'same manifest' vector: V1.

P3.evidence:
- PB -> [1] (T58); PB2 -> [1] (T99); PB3 EXPIRE -> [1] (T97); DRAIN -> [1] HELD (T98).
- With my finer injection (operation record succeeds, DENIED fails), CLOSE, EXPIRE and DRAIN still report [1].
- The oracle compared every CLOSE, EXPIRE and DRAIN report against an independent shadow armed set: 0 mismatches.

P4.evidence:
- PC with RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, with EOF, and revocation followed by a malformed frame -> restart HELD through the marker (T100, T101).
- A torn record forces HELD even when the marker write failed (T102). A failing RESTARTED write -> HELD (T104).
- The residual is reproduced and disclosed (T103).
- Residual search from the closed-clean state (depth 5, 51,170 nodes): 4 divergences, each with at least two journal failures and one marker failure, and none with a marker, a torn record or a durable HELD record.
- Precision of the residual statement: V3.

P5.evidence: Every row has excludeStatus, and the CREATE and DELETE 4xx rows exclude 408. A40 and A41 give M02; A42 (CREATE 422) still agrees. The 'excludeStatus ignored' mutant is caught by A40 and A41. deleteStatus202 cites delete.go:188, the OrphanDependents-false condition, which I verified.

- Tag v1.37.1 resolves to commit f78e722310e50bcaca9276be22276d9e91d91308 (GitHub API, tag object d2b770f).
- All five files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at that commit match the pinned SHA-256 values.

- distributionCheck is stated. A39 (PH) gives M05.

questionAnswers.Q0: P1-P8 are all CLOSED. Every probe named in the brief (PA, PA3, Q3, PD, PE, PB, PB2, PB3, PC, PH) behaves as the README states. Residual items are NOTEs: V1 missing vectors and injection granularity, V2 drain-answer wording and the post-OPEN HELD, V3 residual precision, V4 upstream liveness.
questionAnswers.Q1:
Faithful.
- The v1 files are byte-identical to main 51440c8: git show digests equal source-index for all 15 predecessor inputs. The worktree has only commit 96f340e on top, adding 7 files.
- The v1-to-v2 model diff contains only the P1-P8 changes and the version strings.
- render_request equals v1 and an independent renderer for 69 manifest, verb and UID combinations.
- Carried transcripts differ from v1 exactly as the README lists: T12, T30, T31, T45, T47, T58, T66, T67, T71, T73, T82, plus narrowed intents for T74 and T81. All other differences are the added BIND fields, RESTARTED, failureMarker and the journal digest.
- Only T47 and T82 changed events.
- No v1 safety property weakened. The fuzz and search oracles confirm no unarmed, double or post-invalidation forward, C2/C5 stamps, C7, A4 qualifiers, immutable seals and HELD stickiness.
- Behaviour narrowed on purpose: DRAIN_PENDING only in DRAINING; F01 rather than F00 for depth 17-990; F07 for non-bytes.
- README rationale dropped silently: V5.
questionAnswers.Q3:
No.
- A DELETE needs a UID from this execution's own durable CREATE 201 for that manifest digest.
- Digests and identities are unique across the runs of a configuration, and a run must stay inside the profile.
- MANIFEST_REUSED refuses digests or identities bound in earlier generations.
The shadow-world campaign over three generations, with priorBindings derived only from earlier BIND records, found no create, GET or delete of another run's object. MANIFEST_REUSED is derivable from durable BIND records as stated. The digest half of the check is implied by the identity half.
questionAnswers.Q4:
Only through the disclosed double fault. Every divergence found had at least 2 journal failures and at least 1 marker failure, with no torn record and no durable HELD state record.
- A single journal failure with a failed marker still restarts HELD, through the INVALIDATED record.
- Ambiguous, in-flight or unsealed actions always rebuild HELD.
The residual is accurate against base section 5 in substance. Its wording should name the two journal failures and the 'no later state record' condition, and cover gate-side failures as well as RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED (V3).
questionAnswers.Q5:
Correct.
- Mapping rows, excludeStatus and the 202 note were checked against the pinned Kubernetes source.
- The status rule 'drainPending implies DRAINING or INVALIDATED with an action in flight' is correct. The schema mutant without it is caught by G27, G28 and G30. The rule is never violated by a reachable status, and G29 is accepted.
- MANIFEST_REUSED and UID_NOT_CREATED are in the enums; UID_NOT_OBSERVED is refused (G32).
- Decode codes as stated: F07 for non-bytes, F02 for oversize, F01 for depth including RecursionError, F06 for other decode failures.
- The six I02 outcomes are covered without overloading.

modelExecution.fuzz:
Oracle-driven randomized campaigns with protocol-following and disruptive events across three generations, with priorBindings derived from journals and a shadow API-server world.
- After two oracle bugs of my own were fixed, the final-oracle campaign ran 120 runs: 19,422 events, 360 generations, 141 restarts, 352 forwards, 0 violations.
- An earlier campaign: 48,844 events, 0 violations.
- Larger planned campaigns were cut short by the coordinator's CPU holds.
modelExecution.boundedExhaustive:
Memoized DFS over about 25 abstract events: ARM GET, CREATE and DELETE (own UID, own UID under another manifest, a world UID), OUTCOME, CLOSE (NORMAL, REVOCATION, RR; the other urgent reasons follow the same code path), BACKLOG, ACCEPT, exact and previous-action requests, upstream ok, 500, lost and late, DRAIN, EXPIRE, storage failure plain, torn and fail-second-record, marker failure, EOF, PEER_CHANGED, RESTART, BIND of the next run, malformed frame.
- Depth 4 from all 8 start states (bound; armed with stamp and backlog; CREATE in flight; created and sealed; drain pending in flight; invalidated in flight; closed clean; DELETE armed): 277,405 nodes, 0 violations.
- Depth 6: 15 complete sub-searches, 681,529 nodes, 0 violations. The full depth-6 run was stopped by the coordinator's holds.
- Residual search from closed-clean to depth 5: 51,170 nodes, 4 double-fault divergences, 0 unexplained.

reviewLimit:
Read-only, source-level review by an agent separate from the author. No repository file was created or modified, and no git state change, runner, native, cloud or GitHub mutation took place. Scratch files are only under /private/tmp/claude-501/w02bf-review-r1/.
The conclusions hold within the reference model's abstraction: pre-split request heads, in-memory journals, one-shot failure injection (extended by a reviewer subclass), and no real TLS, HTTP, fsync, clock, broker or I07 handshake.
The search is bounded. Because of the coordinator's CPU holds, the full exhaustive search reached depth 4 for all start states and depth 6 for 15 sub-searches only, and the randomized campaigns were smaller than planned.
Kubernetes behaviour was checked against v1.37.1 source only; the distribution is unselected.
This PASS is not an installed gate, native qualification, a C2/C3 load result or authorization for anything installed. All E01-E12 remain OPEN_UNPROVEN. NOTEs V1-V6 may be carried to W02c-F and the next revision.
